fuel-economy-tracking-sheet.desc: A free one-page printable gas mileage log. Record every fill-up — date, odometer, gallons, cost — and compute MPG yourself with the built-in space. See when your fuel economy drifts.
fuel-economy-tracking-sheet.answer: This is a free, one-page printable fuel log in PDF format. Each row is one fill-up: date, odometer reading, gallons (or liters), price per unit, total cost, and MPG for the tank. When MPG starts drifting down for no obvious reason — tire pressure, air filter, dragging brake — a written log catches it before your dashboard would.
howto: Print the PDF and keep it in the glove box with a pen.
At every fill-up, log date, odometer, gallons, and price — takes ten seconds at the pump.
Subtract the previous odometer to get miles this tank; divide by gallons for MPG.
After a few tanks, you'll have a baseline. Watch for drift downward — that's usually the earliest sign something needs attention.
Keep the sheet for tax records if the vehicle is used for business or self-employed work.
faq: Is this log really free?
Yes. The PDF is free to download and print — no sign-up, no email.
Do I need to fill up to full every time?
For MPG accuracy, yes — 'full-to-full' fill-ups give the cleanest numbers. Partial fills muddy the miles-per-gallon math, though total cost tracking still works.
Why track MPG when the car shows it on the dash?
Dashboard MPG readouts are computed and can drift or reset. A written log is your own baseline — if the car says 30 MPG but your log says 26, the log is usually right.
